newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahraini, Qatari officials hold London talks.
newsitem.headline: Bahraini, Qatari officials hold London talks.

text.p: Senior officials from Bahrain and Qatar, Gulf Arab states locked in a territorial dispute, have held talks in London in an attempt to ease strained relations, a Bahraini official said on Friday.

The official described the meeting on Wednesday between Bahraini Crown Prince Sheikh Hamad bin Isa al-Khalifa and Qatari Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani as a "positive step".
It was their first meeting since Qatar's foreign minister accused Bahrain's crown prince in December of participating in a failed coup attempt in Qatar in February of last year.

Qatar said in February it had arrested 100 people in connection with an anti-government plot involving former bodyguards loyal to the deposed emir Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani, who was overthrown in a bloodless palace coup in 1995 by his son, the current emir.

The Bahraini official said the London meeting "came in the framework of brotherly meetings which help improve relations between the two countries", adding that he hoped such talks would help settle problems.
The territorial dispute between the two countries is centred on small but potentially rich Gulf islands controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Gulf Arab reconciliation efforts have failed to ease tensions between Manama and Doha.
